result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers call the set 'mostly solid' and then raise a long list of issues, so neither fits the rubric's preference for a light-touch pass. A is tighter: it limits must-fix items to three real gaps (focus, on-colors, border contrast), though it still adds many speculative tokens and suggests renaming --ease-out. B goes further: it lists ten items, proposes renames, a new primitive tier and process overhead, and states contrast failures as fact more firmly. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers are long and treat a coherent token set as needing many additions, so neither fully credits what already works. A goes further: it lists five 'fix before v1' items, proposes renaming the motion tokens, and suggests adding a primitive tier. B limits its must-fix list to three real gaps (control border contrast, a focus token, on-colors for status roles), though it also piles on speculative extras and states some contrast results as fact.
